name: Захист від мату: відхід
description:
You know how to defend a piece. And that you can use the same methods to defend against check. You can also use them to defend against checkmate. We start with moving away to escape checkmate.

Sometimes, your king can move away without any problems. Example 1 shows this.
At other times, you need to create a bit of room for the king. This is called making air or luft (the German word for ‘air’).

How this works is shown in exampes 2 and 3.

What do you have to do?
Defend against checkmate by moving away. Play your king or make luft first. Remember: the space you create has to be a propper flight square.

examples.text:
Black’s rook wants to checkmate on the first rank.
White sees through this plan. His king moves to the left, so that he can escape!

Here, moving the king will not help.
Again, Black’s rook moves to the first row to checkmate.
The knight and the rook are taking away the king’s escape squares.

Is there anything White can do to prevent mate? Yes, there is!
He moves the pawn to the third row. The pawn makes ‘luft’.
If Black’s rook checks the king, the king can move away to the square that has been left by the pawn.

Once again the king needs ‘air’. If the rook checks him on the first row, he is trapped. He needs space to be able to get away.

Black’s pawn is a nuicance here.
Stepping aside with the king, or moving up the pawn, is pointless.
The pawn takes away the flight squares.

So, what is White to do?
He takes the annoying black pawn with his own pawn.
The king has luft and is save for now.
